newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY ANNOUNCES DETAILED 1996 ENERGY PRICE HIKES.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY ANNOUNCES DETAILED 1996 ENERGY PRICE HIKES.

text.p: Hungary's Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism (IKIM) on Saturday announced the details of controversial January 1 price increases in the energy sector, in which Western utilities invested over $2 billion last year.

The government announced in November retail hikes of 24.5 percent for electricity and 18.8 percent for gas but did not define the margins which would be granted to individual energy producers and distributors.
The IKIM decrees, published on Saturday, detail the new gas an energy prices, without elaborating on percentage changes for individual companies.

Certain investors earlier expressed dissatisfaction over the January 1 price rises, postponed from October, saying the hikes would not provide the eight precent profit margin the government promised them before the privatisation.
Belgian utility Tractebel said it may even pull out of its investment in the power station Dunamenti.
Investors were not immediately available for comment on the detailed price hikes on Saturday.
A number of western investors, including Germany's RWE and Electricite de France, bought substantial stakes in Hungarian energy companies one year ago.
